kill_fact: The value case's central premise — a KNOWN, DATED, CAPPED impairment (~$360-400M off a ~$1.2B supplemental-Medicaid benefit, phased 2028-2032) leaving a cheap ~6x core — fails independent primary-source verification on three grounds. (1) THE EARNINGS BASE IS MAJORITY POLICY ACCRUAL AND THE CORE IS SHRINKING: per the Q1 2026 10-Q (filed 5/7/26), the aggregate net benefit from all supplemental Medicaid programs was $369M in Q1 2026 vs $236M in Q1 2025 (+56%) against pretax income of $469.1M vs $420.4M — the DPP stream is now ~79% of pretax income and core ex-DPP pretax earnings nearly HALVED year-over-year ($100M vs $184M); the same filing projects a FY2026 aggregate net benefit of $1,362M PLUS a newly approved ~$100M Florida DPP increase (approved April 2026, to be recorded Q2 2026, not yet in the table) — a ~$1.46B run-rate, far more than the '~$1.2B' slice the entire debate was built on. (2) THE IMPAIRMENT IS NO LONGER CAPPED OR DATED: the FY2025 10-K (filed 2/25/26) and Q1 2026 10-Q both RAISED the current-law OBBBA reduction ~20% to $432-480M by 2032 (the debate used the stale mid-2025 $360-400M), and — post-dating the debate entirely — CMS-2449-P (Federal Register 5/22/26, doc 2026-10292) proposes capping ALL state-directed payments at 100% of Medicare rates (110% non-expansion) with phase-downs, extending to ALL SDPs by rating periods on/after 1/1/2029, projecting ~$775B of 10-year savings; UHS's own 10-Q describes its Florida DPP as priced off 'a percentage of average commercial rates' — the exact structure the proposal eliminates. The entire ~$1.46B net benefit is in play, not a $432-480M slice; comments close ~7/21/26. The claimed edge ('the market extrapolates the cliff as if immediate and total') inverts — under the live proposal, near-total IS the current-law-in-progress scenario, and the market is pricing it. (3) HIDDEN DISQUALIFIERS THE DEBATE NEVER MENTIONED: (a) the Cumberland Hospital sexual-abuse mass tort — a standing ~$241M verdict for just the FIRST THREE plaintiffs ($60M compensatory + $180M trebled VCPA + punitives statutorily reduced to $1.05M; on appeal), ~43 ADDITIONAL plaintiffs pending, next trial tentatively AUGUST 2026, with the 10-Q warning that resolution could exhaust the remaining 2020-policy-year insurance and that effective March 2025 the excess commercial coverage 'contains... coverage exclusions for incidents involving sexual molestation or abuse' — a largely uninsured, unreserved fat tail attached to the very behavioral segment carrying the premium multiple; (b) CMS TERMINATED Laurel Ridge (330-bed behavioral, San Antonio; ~$23M 2025 pretax income) from Medicare/Medicaid effective 4/30/26, TRO denied, operating losses expected during reapplication; (c) UHS agreed 3/9/26 to acquire Talkspace for $5.25/sh (~$835M), funded entirely with new credit-agreement borrowings closing Q3 2026 — diverting the buyback capital the value case leaned on (Q1 2026 buyback already slowed to $127.3M, executed at an average $188.54 — 25% above today's price); (d) enhanced ACA premium tax credits EXPIRED 12/31/25 with nothing enacted 'as of early May 2026' per the 10-Q — a live headwind, not a 'scheduled' one. (4) THE DOWNSIDE FLOOR IS GONE ON THE BEAR'S OWN MATH: correcting net debt DOWN to $4.589B (balance-sheet debt $4,708M less $119M cash; the debated $5.01B counts ~$417M of operating leases) helps ~$7/share, but the larger OBBBA cut removes ~$7-8/share and the Talkspace debt draw ~$13/share — corrected bear break ~$148-158 vs $150.58 spot (7/2/26; new 52-week low $140.08 set post-debate), i.e. a ~0-5% cushion before any haircut for Cumberland or CMS-2449-P. A SOFT_EXTENDED thesis now faces only dated NEGATIVE catalysts: NPRM comment close ~7/21/26, Cumberland trial 8/2026, $700M of 1.65% notes maturing 9/1/26 into ~5% refi rates, work requirements 1/2027. The claimed 6:1 reward-to-risk does not survive; the market also rejected a clean Q1 2026 beat (EPS $5.62 vs $5.41 est.) with a -9.4% one-day drop — DPP-composition beats no longer get paid.
